newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Jan trade surplus falls to C$2.10 bln.
newsitem.headline: Canada Jan trade surplus falls to C$2.10 bln.

text.p: Canada's merchandise trade surplus narrowed in January to C$2.10 billion from C$2.84 billion in December (revised from C$2.37 billion), Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
Exports in January rose 3.1 percent to a record C$23.49 billion while imports rose 7.2 percent to a record C$21.40 billion.
Note: Figures in billions of current Canadian dollars, on a balance of payments basis, seasonally adjusted.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of C$2.64 billion in January, with imports of C$20.1 billion and exports of 22.7 billion.

Statistics Canada said a surge in automotive shipments was at the heart of the gain in exports, as car companies moved to replenish dealer inventories in the United States. The growth in non-automotive exports was marginal, the agency said.
Exports to the United States grew the most, but there were gains to all trading partners but the European Union, the agency said.
Imports grew even faster in January, partly because of strong demand for auto parts, machinery and energy products, Statscan said.
The agency said imports were up from all trading partners with the exception of the European Union.
